title: Variable rates of change
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Rates in context, only covers reading steeper as faster on a curve and leaves out the tangent-gradient idea this point teaches, while the instantaneous-rate point uses limits and chords at a deeper level than Stage 5 paths.

draft.title: Variable rates of change
card: On a straight-line graph the rate of change is constant. On a curved graph the rate changes from one place to another.
Where the curve is steeper, the quantity is changing faster. Where it is flatter, the quantity is changing more slowly.
The rate at one moment is the gradient of the tangent there. A tangent is a straight line that just touches the curve at that point.
Example: a tangent to a distance graph touches it at 3 s. It rises 12 m over a run of 4 s. The speed at 3 s is \(12 \div 4 = 3\) m/s.

2.alt: A curve showing the depth of water in a tank in cm against time in minutes. It starts steep and flattens out, passing through the points (0, 0), (2, 6) and (4, 8), and reaching (6, 8.5).

draft.remember: On a curve the rate changes. The rate at a moment is the gradient of the tangent.

a.q: On a curved graph of distance against time, the curve is steepest at 5 s. What does this tell you about 5 s?
opts: The distance is changing fastest around then
The distance is changing slowest around then
The distance is not changing at that time
The rate of change is constant on the whole graph
a.why: A steeper curve means the quantity is changing faster. Slowest change would be where the curve is flattest. A constant rate only happens on a straight line.

b.q: Priya draws a tangent to a graph of a tank's volume (litres) against time (minutes). The tangent touches the curve at 4 min and passes through \((2, 10)\) and \((6, 30)\). What is the rate of change at 4 min?
b.why: The tangent's gradient is the rate: \(\frac{30 - 10}{6 - 2} = \frac{20}{4} = 5\) litres per minute. The tempting 20 is only the rise, and it forgets to divide by the run.
b.clue: Find rise over run for the tangent line.

a.best: The distance is changing fastest around then
